newsitem.title: USA: Techne to restructure unit, sees charge.
newsitem.headline: Techne to restructure unit, sees charge.

text.p: Techne Corp said Monday it will restructure its R&D Systems Europe Ltd subsidiary and as a result take a $450,000 charge that will cut third quarter after-tax earnings by about $0.03 per share.
Techne said it expects to realise operating expense savings in the 1998 fiscal year ending June 30 of about $1.5 million.
The company did not specify whether there would be any layoffs and could not be immediately reached for comment.

R&D Systems Europe, located in Abingdon, England, develops and makes immunoassay kits and molecular biology products and distributes biotechnology products. The restructuring calls for R&D to withdraw from the molecular biology market, Techne said.
Techne said the discontinued molecular biology products represent less than 3 percent of its consolidated revenues and about 9 percent of R&D's revenues.
R&D Managing Director William Finch will leave the company and will be temporarily replaced by Robert Carlson, the unit's director of finance.

"Sales of the discontinued products as a group have been on the decline for over two years and sales of newly developed molecular biology products have not met Techne's expectations. However, RDSE will continue to sell molecular biology products and service those customers until the end of fiscal year 1997," the company said in a release.

It said R&D's remaining activities will be transferred to the company headquarters in Minneapolis during the next three to four months. It said R&D Systems GmbH in Wiesbaden-Nordenstadt, Germany will not be affected, other than to cease selling the discontinued molecular biology products.
"The restructuring will allow Techne to concentrate its world wide marketing and sales efforts on our core cytokine products and improve our overall efficiency" the company said.
